mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% for two consecutive months, labor market tightness triggers a surge in consumer and business confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.0% and remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 30-day historical average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP for two consecutive months indicates excess demand, which accelerates corporate earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth rate exceeds 2% and remains above 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or flat despite the identified PCE acceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in three consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness, lowering investor expectations for future growth and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >3% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 30-day historical average during supply contractions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows accelerating inflation (monthly ΔΔCPI > 0.3% over two months), the Federal Reserve is more likely to raise rates, which reduces the present value of equities and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exhibits accelerating inflation (ΔCPI > 0.3% and Δ²CPI > 0 for two consecutive months)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the inflation signal in the regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) surprise below 50,000 jobs followed by two consecutive months above 50,000, creates a 'labor market softening' pattern that precedes a short-term bearish S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS surprise < 50,000 and the following two months are > 50,000
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the identified pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both unemployment (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 0.5 percentage points and 2% respectively over two consecutive months indicates dual demand-supply pressures that jointly depress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by ≥0.5pp and INDPRO decreases by ≥2% over two consecutive months
regime_hint: dual contraction in labor and supply
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive or flat despite the joint contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by FEDFUNDS > 1% and UNRATE < 4%), the combination of low policy rates and tight labor markets typically supports optimism that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: FEDFUNDS > 1% and UNRATE < 4% for at least 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in the specified regime (p < 0.05).
